description.value: The Agassiz-Harrison Museum & Visitor Centre occupies one of Canada's oldest surviving wood-built Canadian Pacific Railway stations, constructed in 1893 and located in the heart of downtown Agassiz. It serves as both a regional history museum and an official visitor centre for the area, making it a natural waypoint for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley. The on-site Local Motive Giftshop offers locally made artisan goods and country-fresh jams.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms the business is open and operating as a museum and visitor centre in a historic 1893 CPR railway station. OSM phone (604-796-3545) and address (7011 Pioneer Ave) both match the website. The website provides no evidence for bike-specific amenities (parking, racks, water, washrooms), so all cycle-infrastructure fields remain null. The OSM name 'Agassiz Harrison Museum' differs from the website's 'Agassiz-Harrison Museum & Visitor Centre' — hyphen and 'Visitor Centre' designation are missing from OSM.
concerns: OSM name 'Agassiz Harrison Museum' is missing the hyphen and omits '& Visitor Centre' — website name 'Agassiz-Harrison Museum & Visitor Centre' used instead and OSM record should be corrected.
OSM community field lists 'Chilliwack' but the museum is located in Agassiz (District of Kent), not Chilliwack — may cause incorrect geographic grouping in the directory.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, actively operating heritage museum and visitor centre in a historically significant 1893 railway station; the dual museum/visitor-centre role makes it especially useful to touring cyclists seeking local information and points of interest in the Agassiz–Harrison area.
enrichment_extras.notes: No bike-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere on the website; a follow-up contact or site visit would be needed to confirm washrooms, water access, and bike parking availability.
